frame_f461f6452fe5.question: Vulnerability analysis of rDPX V2 Core
artifact_refs: Admin-controlled approvals and privileged state changes
Option purchase integration and payment/accounting flows
DPXETH minting during stake and supply invariants
Authorization, replay protection, and external-call failure handling

history.rationale: WHY NOW: This is the central protocol component, handling privileged approvals, option purchases, staking, and DPXETH minting; flaws here could affect system-wide solvency, token supply, and user funds. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every externally callable state-changing path, verify role checks and approval boundaries, reconcile token/accounting invariants across stake and option flows, inspect oracle and external-call assumptions, and document any confirmed vulnerability or conclude that no exploitable issue is evident.

frame_2541b7472256.question: Vulnerability analysis of Perpetual Atlantic Vault LP
artifact_refs: Two-asset withdrawal accounting and proportional collateral/rDPX payouts
Oracle-priced rDPX share valuation and stale or manipulated price handling
Vault-only collateral update authorization and state synchronization
Share minting, burning, rounding, and insolvency edge cases

history.rationale: WHY NOW: This is a major uncompleted component that controls LP share accounting and withdrawals of both collateral and rDPX, with oracle-dependent valuation and vault-only state updates. These interactions can create direct loss-of-funds or accounting inconsistencies even though the core contract has already been reviewed. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every deposit, mint, burn, withdrawal, collateral update, and oracle-price use; verify authorization, share-price consistency, rounding behavior, stale-price protection, and solvency invariants across all paths, and document any confirmed vulnerability or conclude that no exploitable issue is present.

frame_c5039b026cbb.question: Vulnerability analysis of Perpetual Atlantic Vault
artifact_refs: Option purchase funding and collateral locking
Interaction with the LP contract and oracle-priced values
frame_c5039b026cbb.rationale: WHY NOW: This is an unanalyzed major contract that holds critical collateral and coordinates perpetual option lifecycle operations, making it a high-priority complement to the already analyzed LP component. Its state transitions and cross-contract accounting may expose issues not visible from the LP side, especially around collateral availability, settlement, and privileged controls. EXIT CRITERIA: Review all externally callable state-changing paths and relevant internal transitions; trace collateral, debt, and option-position accounting across deposits, purchases, exercise, settlement, withdrawal, and pause flows; verify authorization and oracle assumptions; conclude with either a concrete vulnerability hypothesis or documented evidence that the key solvency and access-control invariants hold.
